title_en: Supreme People's Court Releases Typical Cases of Drug Crimes
keywords_en: drugs; typical drug crime cases published by the court
full_text_en:
Supreme People's Court Publishes Typical Drug Crime Cases

In recent years, the people's courts have, in accordance with the law, applied penalties to severely punish serious drug crimes, which has played a positive role in curbing the high incidence of drug crimes and achieving a sustained improvement in China's drug control situation. However, under the influence of various domestic and international factors, the drug control situation remains relatively severe. In order to further advance the people's war on drugs and strive for a sustained improvement in China's drug control situation, the people's courts must attach great importance to the trial of drug crime cases, continue to maintain the guiding ideology of overall strict punishment for drug crimes, fully and effectively use the weapon of penalties, and effectively combat, deter, and prevent drug crimes. In terms of policy application, it is necessary, in accordance with the spirit of the "Several Opinions on Implementing the Criminal Policy of Combining Leniency with Severity" issued by the Supreme People's Court at the beginning of this year and the requirements of normative documents such as the "Summary of the Symposium of Some National Courts on the Trial of Drug Crime Cases" issued in 2008, to highlight the focus of the crackdown, and in accordance with the law, severely punish serious drug crimes and criminals such as drug lords, professional drug offenders, recidivists, repeat offenders, and other drug criminals with deep subjective malignancy, high personal danger, and serious harm, as well as those with other serious circumstances. For those whose crimes are extremely serious and who should be sentenced to death according to law, the death penalty must be resolutely imposed in accordance with the law. At the same time, in accordance with the requirements of the criminal policy of combining leniency with severity, differential treatment should be adhered to. For crimes with minor circumstances and relatively small social harm, or where there are statutory or discretionary circumstances for lenient punishment, or where the defendant's subjective malignancy is relatively minor and personal danger is not great, a lenient punishment may be imposed in accordance with the law, so as to split and disintegrate drug criminals, educate and save the majority, attack and isolate the very few, and prevent and reduce drug crimes.

In order to fully reflect the principle position of the people's courts in implementing the requirements of the criminal policy of combining leniency with severity and in applying penalties to severely punish serious drug crimes in accordance with the law, the Supreme People's Court today published five typical drug crime cases in which the death penalty has been approved. The specific case details are as follows:

I. People v. Piao Zhecheng and Luan Haitao — drug trafficking and transportation

From August to December 2007, the defendant Piao Zhecheng purchased a total of approximately 15,000 grams of methamphetamine on six occasions from Song Zhe (at large) in Longjing City, Jilin Province, and transported it to Qingdao City and Yantai City, Shandong Province, to sell to the defendant Luan Haitao. On January 28, 2008, Piao Zhecheng again purchased 3,930 grams of methamphetamine from Song Zhe, intending to transport it to Qingdao to sell to Luan Haitao. On February 2, Piao Zhecheng hid the methamphetamine in apple boxes placed in his Buick business vehicle, and together with his hired driver Jin Changfan (separately prosecuted), took turns driving to Yantai City, and then had Jin Changfan drive alone to Qingdao City. When the vehicle reached the Qingdao toll gate of the Ji-Qing Expressway, public security personnel apprehended Jin Changfan and seized 3,930 grams of methamphetamine from the vehicle on the spot.

The court held that the defendant Piao Zhecheng, knowing it was drugs, trafficked and transported them, and his conduct constituted the crime of drug trafficking and transportation. The defendant Luan Haitao trafficked drugs for illegal profits, and his conduct constituted the crime of drug trafficking. Piao Zhecheng trafficked and transported drugs on multiple occasions, in huge quantities, causing great social harm, and his crimes were extremely serious, thus he should be punished according to law. Luan Haitao trafficked drugs on multiple occasions, in huge quantities. Considering that he had a major meritorious performance after his arrest, a lighter punishment could be imposed according to law, and the death penalty could be imposed but not immediately executed. Accordingly, in accordance with the law, the defendant Piao Zhecheng was sentenced to death and the death penalty was approved, and the defendant Luan Haitao was sentenced to death with a two-year reprieve.

II. People v. Li Mingde — drug transportation

On July 10, 2008, the defendant Li Mingde and Li Mingsheng (separately prosecuted) drove a minivan to pick up drugs from Ruili City, Yunnan Province, and then intended to transport them to Yingjiang County, Yunnan Province. At around 7:00 a.m. that day, Li Mingde and others were apprehended while driving through Longchuan County, Yunnan Province. Public security personnel seized from a woven bag behind the vehicle's seats 18,990.5 grams of heroin, 376.7 grams of opium, and 175.8 grams of methamphetamine.

The court held that the defendant Li Mingde, knowing it was drugs, transported them, and his conduct constituted the crime of drug transportation. Li Mingde transported a huge quantity of drugs, causing great social harm, and his crimes were extremely serious, thus he should be punished according to law. Accordingly, in accordance with the law, the defendant Li Mingde was sentenced to death and the death penalty was approved.

III. People v. Zhang Binglai, Wang Chengyong, et al. — drug trafficking and transportation

In November 2007, the defendant Wang Chengyong went to Huilai County, Guangdong Province, and on three occasions purchased a total of 350 grams of heroin from the defendant Zhang Binglai through the defendant Wu Wensong at a price of RMB 380 or 370 per gram, and transported it back to Quanzhou City, Fujian Province for sale.

In early December of the same year, the defendant Wang Chengyong introduced his drug trading channel to the defendant Wang Kaiqu. Wang Kaiqu paid Wang Chengyong an introduction fee of RMB 10,500. On December 16 of the same month, Wang Chengyong took Wang Kaiqu to Huilai County, Guangdong Province, and through the defendant Wu Wensong, purchased 200 grams of heroin from the defendant Zhang Binglai at a price of RMB 375 per gram. On December 20 of the same month, Wang Chengyong and Wang Kaiqu again purchased 100 grams and 200 grams of heroin respectively from Zhang Binglai through Wu Wensong at a price of RMB 370 per gram. Wang Kaiqu transported the drugs to Quanzhou City, and the two sold them separately. On December 24 of the same month, Wang Kaiqu purchased 202 grams of heroin from Zhang Binglai through Wu Wensong at a price of RMB 370 per gram and 20 "Blue Elf" pills at a price of RMB 80 per pill. At approximately 1:30 a.m. the next day, Wang Kaiqu was apprehended at the long-distance bus station in Jinjiang City, Fujian Province, and the drugs were seized on the spot. On December 29 of the same month, with the cooperation of Wang Kaiqu, the public security organs apprehended Wu Wensong, and later with the cooperation of Wu Wensong, apprehended Zhang Binglai, seizing 63 grams of heroin from Zhang Binglai's car.

In summary, the defendant Zhang Binglai trafficked over 1,115 grams of heroin; Wang Chengyong trafficked and transported over 850 grams of heroin.

The court held that the defendants Zhang Binglai and Wu Wensong, for illegal profits, sold heroin and other drugs to others, and their conduct constituted the crime of drug trafficking; the defendants Wang Chengyong and Wang Kaiqu, for illegal profits, trafficked and transported heroin, and their conduct constituted the crime of drug trafficking and transportation. Zhang Binglai and Wu Wensong trafficked drugs, and Wang Chengyong and Wang Kaiqu trafficked and transported drugs, in large quantities, and a large amount of the drugs had already flowed into society, causing great social harm, thus all should be punished according to law. Wang Chengyong had been sentenced twice before for the crime of drug trafficking, and was a recidivist and repeat drug offender, with deep subjective malignancy and high personal danger, thus a heavier punishment should be imposed according to law. Wang Kaiqu and Wu Wensong had major meritorious performances in assisting in the capture of co-defendants, thus a lighter punishment could be imposed according to law, and the death penalty for the two of them could be imposed but not immediately executed. Accordingly, in accordance with the law, the defendants Zhang Binglai and Wang Chengyong were sentenced to death and the death penalty was approved, and the defendants Wu Wensong and Wang Kaiqu were sentenced to death with a two-year reprieve.

IV. People v. Lin Xing, et al. — drug trafficking and transportation

From late November to mid-December 2006, the defendant Lin Xing followed the defendant Meng Heyu to Maoming City, Guangdong Province on three occasions to purchase a total of 138 grams of heroin, which Lin Xing brought back to Haikou City, Hainan Province, for Meng Heyu to sell.

On February 20 and March 9, 2007, the defendant Lin Xing went to Maoming City twice and purchased a total of 80 grams of heroin, bringing it back to Haikou City; in early March of the same year, Lin Xing purchased 25 grams of heroin in Haikou City. Lin Xing directly or through his girlfriend, the defendant Li Xiaoxue, sold 96 grams of the heroin in several transactions, and the remaining 9 grams of heroin were jointly smoked by Lin Xing and Li Xiaoxue.

In late March 2007, the defendant Lin Xing purchased 10 grams of heroin from another person in Haikou City and sold it to the defendant Meng Heyu.

On April 8, 2007, the defendant Lin Xing went to Maoming City to purchase drugs. The defendant Li Xiaoxue, at Lin Xing's instruction, remitted RMB 44,000 to an account designated by Lin Xing. On April 11 of the same month, Lin Xing purchased a block of heroin, hid it in a rice bag, and transported it to Haikou City by consignment on a long-distance bus, with Lin Xing returning on the same bus. En route, Lin Xing called Li Xiaoxue to contact the bus driver to pick up the goods. In the early morning of the next day, Li Xiaoxue was apprehended as she was about to leave after retrieving the rice bag from the bus. Public security personnel seized a block of heroin on the spot, with a net weight of 330.3 grams.

The court held that the defendant Lin Xing, for illegal profits, repeatedly went to Maoming City to purchase heroin and transport it back to Haikou City for sale, or purchased heroin in Haikou City for sale, and also helped others transport heroin on multiple occasions, and his conduct constituted the crime of drug trafficking and transportation. The defendant Meng Heyu, for illegal profits, repeatedly trafficked and transported heroin, and his conduct constituted the crime of drug trafficking and transportation. The defendant Li Xiaoxue participated in the trafficking of heroin, and her conduct constituted the crime of drug trafficking. Lin Xing trafficked and transported 574.3 grams of heroin, a large quantity, and played a major role in the joint drug trafficking crime with Li Xiaoxue, being the principal offender, and should be punished for all crimes in which he participated, organized, or directed. Meng Heyu trafficked and transported a large quantity of heroin, and should be punished according to law. Li Xiaoxue played a supporting role in the joint crime, being an accessory, and had meritorious performance, thus her punishment should be mitigated according to law. Accordingly, in accordance with the law, the defendant Lin Xing was sentenced to death and the death penalty was approved, and the defendants Meng Heyu and Li Xiaoxue were sentenced to life imprisonment and fixed-term imprisonment of ten years, respectively.

V. People v. Li Zheng and Ma Mochengmei — drug trafficking and transportation

In early August 2004, the wife of the defendant Li Zheng, Lama Molihuo, together with Aermozizuo (both separately convicted and sentenced), conspired to traffic heroin. Aermozizuo contacted the supply source, and Lama Molihuo invited E Dilasha and Li You (both separately convicted and sentenced) to assist in carrying the drugs. On August 12 of the same year, Li Zheng drove a Santana sedan and went with the aforementioned four persons to Yanyuan County, Sichuan Province, to purchase heroin. Lama Molihuo and Aermozizuo purchased 4 blocks of heroin and handed them to E Dilasha and Li You, who took a long-distance bus to transport them back to Xichang City, Sichuan Province. At approximately 11:00 a.m. the next day, Li Zheng drove with Lama Molihuo and Aermozizuo along the Mopanshan section of National Highway 307 when they encountered a public security inspection. Li Zheng accelerated to flee, made Lama Molihuo and Aermozizuo get out of the car and hide, and then abandoned the car and absconded. At around 3:00 p.m. that day, Lama Molihuo and Aermozizuo were apprehended in Xichang City while handing over the drugs to E Dilasha. Public security personnel seized 4 blocks of heroin on the spot, with a net weight of 1,386 grams.

In 2007, the defendant Li Zheng conspired with the defendant Ma Mochengmei and Ze Ritu (deceased due to illness) to traffic heroin. In early August of the same year, the three arrived at Menglian Dai Lahu Va Autonomous County (hereinafter referred to as Menglian County), Yunnan Province. Ze Ritu purchased 2 blocks of heroin from another person and hid them in a house rented by the three. On September 28 of the same year, Ma Mochengmei carried a travel bag containing the heroin and took a long-distance bus to Kunming City, Yunnan Province. The next day, she completed the procedures for consigning the bag to Xichang City. On October 2 of the same year, Ma Mochengmei was apprehended when she went to collect the bag in Xichang City, and Li Zheng and Ze Ritu were also apprehended in Menglian County. The next day, at Ma Mochengmei's indication, public security personnel seized 2 blocks of heroin from the consigned woven bag, with a net weight of 721.5 grams.

The court held that the defendants Li Zheng and Ma Mochengmei, for illegal profits, conspired with others to traffic and transport heroin, and their conduct constituted the crime of drug trafficking and transportation. Li Zheng trafficked and transported 2,107.5 grams of heroin, a large quantity, acted actively in the joint crime, and continued to commit drug crimes while a wanted fugitive, indicating deep subjective malignancy and high personal danger, thus he should be punished according to law. Ma Mochengmei trafficked and transported a large quantity of drugs and acted actively in the joint crime, thus she should also be punished according to law. Accordingly, in accordance with the law, the defendant Li Zheng was sentenced to death and the death penalty was approved, and the defendant Ma Mochengmei was sentenced to life imprisonment.

The criminals Piao Zhecheng, Li Mingde, Zhang Binglai, Wang Chengyong, Lin Xing, and Li Zheng, who were legally sentenced to death and whose death penalties were approved in the above five cases, have been executed recently.
